title: I’d Rather Know Now
scene: You have made a good start on a piece of work, but before going much further you want to confirm that the overall direction is right. You invite early feedback so changes can still be made without too much extra work.
sceneJa: ある程度作業を進めたところで、これ以上大きく進める前に方向性が合っているか確認したい場面。完成後の大きな手戻りを避けるため、早めにフィードバックを求める。

chunks.ja: 順調にスタートできています

chunks.en: but I’d like to make sure
chunks.ja: ただ、確認しておきたいです

chunks.en: I’m heading in the right direction
chunks.ja: 正しい方向へ進んでいることを
これ以上大きく進める前に
もし何か懸念があるなら
全体的な進め方について
今聞いておきたいです
全部完成してからよりも
まだ十分早い段階なので

chunks.en: without causing too much extra work.
chunks.ja: あまり大きな追加作業を発生させずに済みます

chunks.en: Once we agree on the direction,
chunks.ja: 方向性について合意できれば

questions.question: Which chunking is most natural?
options: I’d rather hear them now / than after everything is finished
I’d rather / hear them now than / after everything / is finished
I’d / rather hear / them now than after / everything is finished
questions.explanation: ‘I’d rather hear them now’ forms the preferred option, and ‘than after everything is finished’ gives the alternative being compared.

questions.question: What does ‘before I go much further’ mean here?
options: Before progressing much further with the work
questions.explanation: Here ‘go much further’ means continuing the work substantially, not physical movement.

questions.question: Why does the speaker want feedback now?
options: Because changes can still be made with relatively little rework
Because the work is already finished
Because the speaker does not want to make any decisions
questions.explanation: The speaker wants to catch a possible mismatch while it is still cheap and easy to correct.

speak: Sound open to feedback rather than nervous. Start ‘I’ve made a good start’ positively, slow slightly at ‘heading in the right direction’, give a little emphasis to ‘hear them now’, and finish ‘move ahead with more confidence’ with a settled, forward-looking tone.
review: Previous session: compare alternatives after an unexpected delay. Useful chunks were ‘be in a rush’, ‘would have involved ...’, and ‘be better off -ing’. Today shifts from choosing between options to checking direction before committing more work. Useful chunks are ‘head in the right direction’, ‘I’d rather hear it now than later’, and ‘Once we agree on the direction, ...’.
